howIBuild.heading: How I build
howIBuild.subheading: Three claims. You can check all three without leaving this page.

keyboard.title: Keyboard first
keyboard.description: Put the mouse down and press Tab. Every focus ring is visible, the skip link works, and nothing traps you. Contrast holds in both themes.
keyboard.check: Check it: press Tab, right now.

lean.title: Nothing loads that doesn't have to
lean.description: No animation library, no carousel, no hero video, no font CDN. One third-party script (Vercel Analytics) and nothing else. Fonts are self-hosted through next/font with a single file preloaded. Turn JavaScript off and the words on this page are still here; they are rendered on the server.
lean.check: Check it: open the Network tab and reload.

open.title: Open where it can be
open.description: TypeScript strict in every TypeScript project, and no ts-ignore anywhere in the public repos. Three of the eight projects have public repos. Read the source instead of taking my word for it. The client work is private, and the project cards say exactly what is being held back and why.

projects.heading: Projects
projects.subheading: Three built for paying clients, three built for me, plus two demo sites for small businesses. The client ones are in daily use.

stack.heading: Stack
stack.subheading: What I reach for. The detail is on the project pages.

finalCta.heading: Hiring, or have a system that needs building?
finalCta.subheading: Full-time roles and contract work both. If you have a process running on a spreadsheet that four people are editing at once, that is the thing I build.

services.heading: What I build
services.subheading: Three kinds of site. We start from whichever fits.

realEstate.title: Real estate site with a listing panel
realEstate.description: Your listings on your own site, on a map and on Google. You add a new listing from the panel yourself: photos, price, rooms, location. A buyer writes to you from the WhatsApp button under the listing.

highlights.1: Unlimited listings from your own panel
highlights.3: Every listing is its own page on Google

brochure.title: Business website
brochure.description: A single address that opens properly on a phone and shows up on Google and Google Maps. Your services, photos, opening hours and directions. This is the link you put in your Instagram bio.

highlights.1: Up to five pages, works on phones
highlights.3: The domain is registered in your name

booking.title: WhatsApp appointments
booking.description: The customer picks a day and time on the site, and the request lands in your WhatsApp as a message. No separate app, no separate monthly fee. You still confirm the appointment yourself.

examples.heading: Examples
examples.subheading: Two demos and one live site. Click through them.

yenigun.title: Yenigün Emlak
yenigun.summary: A real estate agency in Sakarya. I built the interface; 150+ listings are live. Listing filters and the agency's own listing panel.

ritim.title: Ritim Fitness
ritim.summary: One page for a neighbourhood gym: membership prices, the weekly class schedule, opening hours and a membership request over WhatsApp.
ritim.imageAlt: Ritim Fitness home page with membership prices and the weekly schedule

salon.title: Aura Beauty Studio
salon.summary: A one-page salon site. The booking button opens WhatsApp, three colour options, and a booking bar pinned to the bottom of the screen on phones.
salon.imageAlt: Aura Beauty Studio hero with the TR/EN toggle and three theme dots in the header

howItWorks.heading: How it works
howItWorks.subheading: From the first call to going live, three steps. You never touch the technical side.

1.label: We talk
1.description: On the phone or WhatsApp, about what you need. Price and timeline arrive in writing.

2.label: You see a draft
2.description: I send the first version as a link. You say what to change, and it changes.

3.label: It goes live
3.description: The site launches on your own domain, with the Google listing and the WhatsApp link ready.
